_usage: GRV Riddles & Brain Teasers rounds (campaign overlay games). Boards pick `count` items per round from a seeded per-day permutation. kind = riddle | teaser; q <= 150 chars; a <= 40 chars; why <= 120 chars. Family-friendly, fair, solvable in ~20 s; run tools/lint_games.py before shipping.

items.q: What has 88 keys but can't open a single lock?
items.why: Its keys play notes, not open doors.

items.q: What hangs on the wall and has hands but can't clap?
items.why: Its hands point to the hour and the minute.

items.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
items.why: The more it dries you, the more water it holds.

items.q: What has a neck and a collar but no head?
items.why: Shirts have both, and no head of their own.

items.q: What has teeth but never bites, and keeps your hair neat?
items.why: Its teeth glide through hair instead of food.

items.q: What has four legs, never walks, and holds your plate at dinner?
items.why: It stands all day and goes nowhere.

items.q: What has a spine and pages but isn't a person?
items.why: A book's spine holds all its pages together.

items.q: What has a mouth and a bed but never eats or sleeps?
items.why: It flows out of its mouth into the sea, and runs along its bed.

items.q: What runs when you turn its handle but never leaves the sink?
items.why: Water runs from it, but the faucet stays put.

items.q: What goes up when the rain comes down?
items.why: You open it as the first drops fall.

items.q: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
items.why: Every step you take leaves another print.

items.q: What belongs to you but other people use more than you do?
items.why: Everyone else says it far more often than you do.

items.q: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a week?
items.why: Look at the spelling of each word: minute has one M, moment has two.

items.q: What word gets shorter when you add two letters to it?
items.why: Add "er" and you get "shorter".

items.q: What building has the most stories?
items.why: Stories, as in tales, not floors.

items.q: What has a thumb and four fingers but isn't alive?
items.why: It has a spot for each finger and your thumb.

items.q: What can travel around the world while staying in one corner?
items.why: It sits in the corner of the envelope the whole way there.

items.q: What flies without wings and cries without eyes?
items.why: It drifts across the sky and rains.

items.q: What has a head and a tail but no body?
items.why: Heads on one side, tails on the other.

items.q: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
items.why: Dig out more dirt and the hole grows.

items.q: What invention lets you look right through a wall?
items.why: It's a see-through gap in the wall.

items.q: What has teeth but never eats, and holds your jacket closed?
items.why: Its little teeth lock together to close the jacket.

items.q: What starts with T, ends with T, and is full of T?
items.why: It starts and ends with the letter T, and it holds tea.

items.q: What starts with E, ends with E, and holds just one letter?
items.why: Envelope starts and ends with E, and it holds a letter.

items.q: What is full of holes but still holds water?
items.why: The holes soak up water and keep it inside.

items.q: What can fill a whole room but takes up no space?
items.why: Switch it on and the room fills, and nothing moves in.

items.q: What goes all the way around a yard but never moves?
items.why: It circles the yard and stays right where it is.

items.q: What is always in front of you but can't be seen?
items.why: It's always ahead of you, and you can't see it yet.

items.q: What has a tongue and laces but never talks?
items.why: The tongue sits under the laces and says nothing.

items.q: What green vegetable has a heart in the middle and leaves you pull off one by one?
items.why: Peel away its leaves and you reach the soft heart.

items.q: What has ears but cannot hear?
items.why: An ear of corn grows on a stalk.

items.q: What has one head, one foot, and four legs?
items.why: A bed has a head, a foot and four legs.

items.q: What goes up and down but never moves?
items.why: The steps rise and fall, but the stairs stay put.

items.q: What hangs in a classroom, starts out dark, and fills up with chalk writing?
items.why: Teachers write on its dark surface with chalk and wipe it off after.

items.q: What fuzzy yellow thing gets served but never eaten?
items.why: A serve starts the point in tennis.

items.q: What kind of band holds a rolled-up newspaper but never plays music?
items.why: It stretches and holds things together instead.

items.q: What has a foot but no legs, and helps you draw straight lines?
items.why: A ruler is 12 inches long, which makes one foot.

items.q: What is made of water but floats on water?
items.why: Ice is lighter than liquid water, so it floats.

items.q: What falls from the clouds in drops and fills puddles on the ground?
items.why: When cloud droplets get heavy enough, they fall as rain.

items.q: What has twelve months on it but is only good for one year?
items.why: Each new year needs a fresh one on the wall.

items.q: What sits right in the middle of both March and April?
items.why: MARCH and APRIL have five letters each, and R is third in both.

items.q: What month has 28 days?
items.why: Every month has at least 28 days.

items.q: What is always coming but never arrives?
items.why: It's always a day away, and when it comes it's called today.

items.q: What must be broken before you can cook with it?
items.why: You break the shell to cook what's inside.

items.q: What is bought by the yard but walked on?
items.why: Carpet is sold by the yard and goes on the floor.

items.q: What can you tell, play on a friend, and laugh at?
items.why: You tell a joke, play a joke, and laugh at a good one.

items.q: What kind of coat is always wet when you put it on?
items.why: Fresh paint is wet when it goes on the wall.

items.q: What has cities with no houses, mountains with no trees, and water with no fish?
items.why: It shows all of those, drawn on paper.

items.q: What gets shorter every time you sharpen it?
items.why: Each sharpening shaves off a little more wood and lead.

items.q: What has many keys but no locks, and a space bar but no room?
items.why: You type on its keys and press the space bar.

items.q: I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old. What am I?
items.why: It burns down a little more each hour.

items.q: What falls in winter without ever getting hurt?
items.why: Snow floats down softly and lands as a fluffy blanket.

items.q: What kind of tree can you carry in your hand?
items.why: Your palm is the inside of your hand.

items.q: What is full of holes but can still catch fish?
items.why: The holes let water through and keep the fish in.

items.q: What has a spout and a handle and sings when it's hot?
items.why: It whistles when the water boils.

items.q: What bird also lifts steel beams at building sites?
items.why: Cranes are birds, and cranes are also the tall machines on job sites.

items.q: What animal can jump higher than a house?
items.why: A house can't jump at all.

items.q: What loses its head every morning but gets it back at night?
items.why: You lift your head off it each morning and lay it back at night.

items.q: What has layers and makes your eyes water when you chop it?
items.why: Chopping it lets out a gas that stings your eyes.

items.q: What has a hole in the middle, comes glazed or sprinkled, and goes well with coffee?
items.why: It's a sweet ring of dough with the hole built in.

items.q: What can you hold in your left hand but never in your right?
items.why: It's attached to the right arm, so only the left can hold it.

items.q: What arches across the sky in seven colors but can never be touched?
items.why: It appears when sun shines through rain, and you can't reach it.

items.q: What always points north but never travels?
items.why: Its pointer swings to north and stays there.

items.q: What has six strings but can't tie a single knot?
items.why: Its strings make music, not knots.

items.q: What has a bridge, four strings and a bow, tucks under your chin, and crosses no river?
items.why: A violin's bridge holds up the strings.

items.q: What has a bell, a mouthpiece, and a slide?
items.why: Slide it in and out to change the note.

items.q: What follows lightning but arrives a little late?
items.why: Light travels faster than sound, so you hear thunder after the flash.

items.q: What floats like a feather, shines with rainbow colors, and pops when you grab it?
items.why: It's a thin film of soapy water wrapped around air.

items.q: What has a peak and a foot but never walks?
items.why: The peak is the top and the foot is the base.

items.q: What has rings inside that tell you how old it is?
items.why: Each year adds one ring to the trunk.

items.q: What rises every morning without an alarm clock?
items.why: It comes up all by itself each day.

items.q: What changes shape through the month but stays in the sky?
items.why: It goes from crescent to full and back.

items.q: I carry my house on my back, leave a shiny trail, and move slowly. What am I?
items.why: Its shell is its home and the trail is slime.

items.q: I'm a bird in a black-and-white suit that swims but can't fly. What am I?
items.why: Penguins use their wings as flippers.

items.q: What has a hood, a trunk, and a horn but isn't an animal?
items.why: Every car has all three.

items.q: What has a tail and stays up by catching the wind?
items.why: The wind lifts it while you hold the string.

items.q: What has a crown and a brim but isn't royal?
items.why: It's the top part and the edge of a hat.

items.q: What has a cap but no head, and writes with a tiny rolling ball?
items.why: A ballpoint pen rolls ink out through a tiny ball at its tip.

items.q: What has a seat, a back, and arms but never gets up?
items.why: It holds you up and never stands.

items.q: What stands by the road, fills up with letters, and can't read a single one?
items.why: Letters go in, but it never opens one.

items.q: What gets smaller every time you use it with water?
items.why: It wears away a little with each wash.

items.q: What can't talk but answers when you speak?
items.why: It repeats your own words back.

items.q: What bean is never grown in a garden?
items.why: It's made of sugar in a candy factory.

items.q: What follows you around in the sun but vanishes when it's cloudy?
items.why: It needs a light to appear.

items.q: What is taller sitting down than standing up?
items.why: When a dog sits, its head is up taller than when it stands on all fours.

items.q: What hangs from the roof in winter and melts in the sun?
items.why: It forms from dripping water that freezes and grows downward.

items.q: I'm round and flat, I spin, and I play music when an arm touches me. What am I?
items.why: The arm follows its grooves to play the music.

items.q: What disappears the moment you say its name?
items.why: Speaking breaks it.

items.q: What do you throw out when you want to use it and pull in when you're done?
items.why: You drop it overboard to stay put and haul it up to leave.

items.q: What big bird scoops up fish in a stretchy pouch under its beak?
items.why: The pouch scoops up fish and water, then drains the water out.

items.q: I wear a yellow coat that you peel off, and I'm soft and sweet inside. What am I?
items.why: The yellow coat is the peel.

items.q: Bees make me, I'm golden and sticky, and I go on toast. What am I?
items.why: Bees make it from flower nectar.

items.q: What bird can fly backwards?
items.why: It beats its wings so fast it can go in any direction.

items.q: I'm orange, I grow underground, and rabbits love me. What am I?
items.why: It's a root vegetable.

items.q: What fruit wears a crown and a spiky coat?
items.why: The leafy crown sits on top of a spiky skin.

items.q: What has arms that spin in the wind but never goes anywhere?
items.why: Its blades turn in the breeze.

items.q: What has a handle but no door and holds your morning coffee?
items.why: It's a cup with a handle.

items.q: What has a saddle but no horse?
items.why: You sit on its saddle and pedal.

items.q: What sits on your nose and has two lenses?
items.why: They help you see clearly.

items.q: What has no beginning and no end, no matter where you start tracing it?
items.why: Its line loops back on itself, with no first or last point.

items.q: What measures 36 inches and has three feet but can't walk?
items.why: Three 12-inch feet make one yard.

items.q: What goes in the toaster flat and pops out warm and golden?
items.why: The toaster makes it toast.

items.q: What can push a sailboat and fly a kite but is invisible?
items.why: You only see what it moves.

items.q: What has a shaggy head, a long handle, and leaves the floor shiny?
items.why: Dip it in the bucket, then swish it across the floor.

items.q: What has a handle and wheels, and you pack it before you travel?
items.why: It holds your clothes while you travel.

items.q: What number comes next: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
items.why: Each number doubles.

items.q: Find the next number: 1, 4, 9, 16, ...
items.why: These are square numbers: 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, so 5x5.

items.q: Keep this going: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...
items.why: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: Continue the countdown: 99, 88, 77, 66, ...
items.why: Each number drops by 11.

items.q: Which number follows 2, 3, 5, 7, 11?
items.why: These are the prime numbers in order.

items.q: Finish the pattern: 1, 3, 6, 10, ...
items.why: The jumps grow by one each time: +2, +3, +4, then +5.

items.q: Which day is next: Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun, Tue, ...?
items.why: Skip a day each time, looping through the week: Tue, then Thu.

items.q: Which letter is next: J, F, M, A, M, J, ...?
items.why: They are the first letters of the months: July comes next.

items.q: Which letter is next: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, E, ...?
items.why: They start the numbers one to eight, so nine comes next.

items.q: How many sides do two triangles have all together?
items.why: Each triangle has three sides, and 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: A farmer has 17 sheep, and all but 9 wander off. How many are left?
items.why: All but 9 means 9 stay.

items.q: How many times can you take 5 away from 25?
items.why: After the first time it is 20, not 25.

items.q: Double my number and add 4 to get 20. What's my number?
items.why: Double 8 is 16, and 16 + 4 = 20.

items.q: Two coins make 30 cents, and one of them isn't a nickel. What are they?
items.why: One isn't a nickel, but the other one is.

items.q: How many months have 31 days?
items.why: January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

items.q: A clock takes 5 seconds to strike 6. How long does it take to strike 12?
items.why: Six strikes have 5 gaps of 1 second, and twelve have 11 gaps.

items.q: A bat and a ball cost $1.10, and the bat costs $1 more than the ball. How much is the ball?
items.why: Ball 5 cents, bat $1.05: that's $1.10 total and $1 apart.

items.q: What letter completes this: A, C, E, G, ...?
items.why: It skips a letter each time.

items.q: Which letter is next: Z, Y, X, W, ...?
items.why: The alphabet runs backwards.

items.q: Spot the rule and continue: 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ...
items.why: The jumps grow: +1, +2, +3, +4, then +5.

items.q: What number comes next: 64, 32, 16, 8, ...?
items.why: Each number is cut in half.

items.q: Name the next number: 3, 9, 27, ...
items.why: Each number is multiplied by 3.

items.q: What follows 2, 5, 8, 11?
items.why: Each number goes up by 3.

items.q: Count along: 7, 14, 21, 28, ...
items.why: Count by sevens.

items.q: What is the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, ...?
items.why: The jumps are +4, +6, +8, so next is +10.

items.q: Complete the sequence: A1, B2, C3, D4, ...
items.why: The letters and the numbers both go up by one.

items.q: Look for the rule: 1, 8, 27, 64, ...
items.why: These are cubes: 1x1x1, 2x2x2, up to 5x5x5.

items.q: Count by twelves: 12, 24, 36, 48, ...
items.why: 48 + 12 = 60, which is five dozen.

items.q: A rooster lays an egg on top of a pointed roof. Which way does it roll?
items.why: Roosters don't lay eggs.

items.q: Which is heavier: a pound of feathers or a pound of bricks?
items.why: Both weigh one pound.

items.q: How far can a runner go into the woods?
items.why: After halfway, the runner is running back out.

items.q: Sam's mom has four kids: April, May, June, and one more. What's the fourth one called?
items.why: Sam's mom has four kids, and Sam is one of them.

items.q: A red house is made of red bricks, a blue house of blue bricks. What is a greenhouse made of?
items.why: A greenhouse is a glass building for plants.

items.q: You're in a race and pass the person in second place. What place are you in?
items.why: You took their spot, but the leader is still ahead.

items.q: Two fathers and two sons go fishing and catch three fish, one each. How?
items.why: A grandfather, his son, and his grandson.

items.q: Add the missing number: 5, 10, 20, 40, ...
items.why: Each number doubles.

items.q: What can you put in a barrel to make it lighter?
items.why: A hole takes away material, so it weighs less.

items.q: Three bakers make 3 pies in 3 hours. How many bakers make 100 pies in 100 hours?
items.why: Each baker makes 1 pie every 3 hours, so 3 bakers make 1 an hour: 100 in 100 hours.

items.q: If today is Wednesday, what day was it the day before yesterday?
items.why: Yesterday was Tuesday, so the day before was Monday.

items.q: A ship's rope ladder has 8 rungs underwater. The tide rises 4 feet. How many rungs are underwater now?
items.why: The ship floats up with the tide, so the same 8 rungs stay under.

items.q: How can a person go 8 days without sleep?
items.why: They stay awake all 8 days and do all their sleeping at night.

items.q: Which shape is next: triangle, square, pentagon, ...?
items.why: Sides go up by one: 3, 4, 5, then 6.

items.q: Which number is next: 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, ...?
items.why: These are the days in January through May, so June has 30.

items.q: Half of my number plus 5 makes 15. What's my number?
items.why: Half of 20 is 10, and 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Two digits add to 9 and multiply to 20. What are they?
